cards.alt: Sample multiple choice card: Which change would increase the rate of O2 diffusion across the respiratory membrane?

questions.stem: A patient with pulmonary fibrosis has a normal alveolar PO2 but a low arterial PO2. What is the best explanation?
options: A thickened alveolar-capillary membrane slows O2 diffusion
questions.explanation: Fick's law says diffusion falls as membrane thickness increases, so equilibration is incomplete and PaO2 lags behind alveolar PO2. Surfactant loss lowers compliance, dead space affects ventilation not diffusion, and carbonic anhydrase handles CO2.

questions.stem: A patient on warfarin has a prolonged INR. Which clotting factor is NOT reduced?
questions.explanation: Warfarin blocks vitamin K recycling, lowering the vitamin K-dependent factors II, VII, IX and X. Factor VIII is not vitamin K dependent.

questions.stem: A mouse lacks functional MHC II. Which defect is expected?
options: Failure to present antigen to CD8 T cells
Poor help for B cells, with little class switching
questions.explanation: MHC II presents peptide to CD4 helper cells, which drive B cell class switching and memory. CD8 cells use MHC I, NK cells and complement do not require MHC II.
questions.subtopic: Adaptive immunity: T cells and MHC

questions.stem: Which structure senses distal tubular NaCl and regulates the afferent arteriole?
questions.explanation: The macula densa signals tubuloglomerular feedback and renin release. Podocytes form the filtration slits, vasa recta preserve the gradient, and principal cells respond to ADH and aldosterone.

questions.stem: An organophosphate pesticide inhibits acetylcholinesterase. What happens at the neuromuscular junction?
options: ACh persists and the end plate stays depolarized, causing fasciculations then paralysis
ACh release is blocked, causing flaccid paralysis
Ca2+ release from the SR is blocked
questions.explanation: Persistent ACh keeps the end plate depolarized and desensitized. Botulinum toxin blocks release, curare blocks receptors, and dantrolene-type drugs affect SR Ca2+ release.

demo_cards.front: Trace the path of air from the nose to the alveoli.
demo_cards.back: Nasal cavity, pharynx, larynx, trachea, primary bronchi, smaller bronchi, bronchioles, alveolar ducts, alveoli.

demo_cards.text: The conducting zone runs from the nose to the {{c1::terminal bronchioles}} and has no gas exchange; the respiratory zone begins with the {{c2::respiratory bronchioles}}.
demo_cards.extra: The conducting zone is the anatomic dead space, about 150 mL.

demo_cards.stem: About what partial pressure of O2 (mmHg) is found in alveolar air at sea level?
demo_cards.why: Alveolar PO2 is about 100 mmHg. Inspired dry air is about 160 mmHg, 760 is total atmospheric pressure, and 40 is typical venous PO2.

demo_cards.statement: Goblet cell mucus and ciliary beating move trapped particles up toward the pharynx (the mucociliary escalator).
demo_cards.why: Cilia sweep the mucus layer upward; smoke paralyzes cilia and raises infection risk.
